explanation: A structure in C is a user-defined data type that groups variables of different types into a single unit. It is used to organize complex data, improve code readability, and facilitate data handling in programs, such as passing multiple values as a single entity.
syntax: struct struct_name { type member1; type member2; ... };
example_explanation: This example defines a structure named myarg_t with two integer members, a and b. In the main function, an instance of the structure is created, values are assigned to its members, and the values are printed to the console, demonstrating how structures group and access related data in a simple and organized way.
